turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, sit wherever's comfy. How's the baby been treating you this week?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're thirty weeks now, is that right?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We were late, umm, the parking garage was full and i circled like ten minutes.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): No worries at all. What brought you in today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Creeping legs at night. Three weeks.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. And how's your sleep been with that?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Awful.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's up pacing the hall around two, rubbing her calves, most nights i stay over.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): That sounds exhausting. Are your ankles puffing up at all?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you had any fever?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or trouble catching your breath?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about headaches?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Sometimes. Not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. What medicines are you taking?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Feros sulfate. Folic acid.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oh good, so that's ferrous sulfate 325 milligrams once a day by mouth for the low iron, and folic acid one milligram every morning by mouth for the pregnancy?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the magnesium, or the colace, did either of those get going?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Stopped the magnessium in March. Never took colace.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Got it. Tell me about your family's health, anybody with sugar or pressure or anything like that?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar, and grandma had a stroke.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thanks, that's helpful. And a normal week for you, work, food, moving around, drinking?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I cashier at the market, umm about twelve hours a week, i eat cereal and takeout mostly, i walk the dog a little, and i don't drink any alcohol.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): You said no ankle swelling. Has that stayed true in the evenings?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Well actually they puff up at night.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, let me look. Calves are soft, not tender, no redness, and i don't see any swelling right now. Pressure today is 118 over 74, pulse eighty six.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your ferritin earlier in the pregnancy was, uh, nine, sorry, eleven. That's low. I'm going to order a repeat ferritin and a cbc.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I think this is restless legs, probably from the low iron while you're pregnant. Keep the iron and the folic acid going, stretch your calves before bed, and skip the late caffeine. Your midwife check is already booked for next week. If one leg gets hot or suddenly huge, call us.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok.

spec.situation: Pregnant woman at 30 weeks with creeping legs at night and poor sleep; ferritin discussed; takes folic acid and iron; midwife check booked.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Poor sleep is supported; 'severe' is not explicitly stated.
bad.text: poor sleep (category=neurological, status=present, severity=severe, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Patient denied ankle swelling initially when asked ('No'), before later clarifying that ankles puff up at night.
Headaches were equivocal/minimized ('Sometimes. Not really'), not a clear positive headache symptom.
Physical exam noted calves were soft.
No swelling was seen at the time of examination ('i don't see any swelling right now'), specifically despite nighttime puffiness history.
Earlier in pregnancy ferritin was 11 (doctor corrected from 9 to 11) and was low.
Follow-up was specifically that the midwife check was already booked for next week.
